title: clip
body:
## clip

Cuts the input with a plane through origin with normal normal and keeps one side, returning an unstructured grid of whole and cut cells (dimension is kept, unlike slice). With the Schemaxis default invert false the kept half is the side the normal points into; true keeps the opposite side. Use it to open a volume for viewing interior fields; use pvClip for box, sphere, cylinder or scalar clips and for crinkle (whole-cell) clipping.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- ParaView's own Clip starts with Invert on (keeping the side opposite the normal); Schemaxis sets invert false by default, so results can be mirrored relative to a ParaView GUI session.
- Clipping structured data produces an unstructured grid, which can use much more memory.

Native constructor: `Clip`. Identity: `curated binding`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the dataset on which the Clip filter will operate. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet); hyper-tree grids (adaptive AMR-like trees) (vtkHyperTreeGrid). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet","vtkHyperTreeGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `origin` | A point lying on the cutting plane, expressed as [X, Y, Z] in dataset coordinates. Moving it along the normal moves the cut. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `normal` | Direction perpendicular to the plane. Use z+ for an XY plane, y+ for XZ, and x+ for YZ; a nonzero XYZ vector or declared direction object also works. | `{"type":"union","title":"direction","summary":"An axis token, a vector, or an azimuth and elevation about an up axis","options":[{"type":"string","title":"axis token such as 'x+' or 'z-'"},{"type":"array","title":"vector [x, y, z]","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3},{"type":"object","title":"direction object","properties":{"axis":{"type":"string","summary":"Axis token such as 'x+'"},"azimuth":{"type":"number","minimum":-360,"maximum":360,"summary":"Degrees about the up axis from the reference axis"},"elevation":{"type":"number","minimum":-180,"maximum":180,"summary":"Degrees tilted from the plane perpendicular to up"},"vector":{"type":"array","title":"vector [x, y, z]","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3},"up":{"type":"union","title":"up direction","options":[{"type":"string","title":"axis token such as 'z+'"},{"type":"array","title":"vector [x, y, z]","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}]}}}]}` | `[1,0,0]` | `[1,0,0]` |
| `invert` | Reverse which side of the plane is retained. Check the result against the plane normal in a preview. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` | `false` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "clip",
  "inputs": {
    "input": "UPSTREAM_input"
  }
}
```
